_common.semantics: c is a deep frozen copy; every object/array is a STRICT facade: reading an absent key is a refusal (policy broken), array non-index keys strict, an index past the end reads undefined; == and != refused at parse; number<string ordering refused; result must be boolean or the policy is broken. Absent OPTIONAL fields (e.g. paths[i].topLevel when no roots given) are therefore refusals, not undefined.

fields.has: (op: Op, kind?: ResourceKind) => boolean (throws on an op/kind outside the algebra)
fields.uses: (name: string) => boolean (throws on a non-string or empty name)

effects.on_unknown: unknown=true; pairs = every Op over the unknown resource; reads/writes = [unknown resource]; has()/uses() always true

Resource_fields.where: src/effects.ts:54 (RESOURCE_FIELDS); every resource carries ALL of them, absent ones undefined

fields.effects: EffectSet view; fromFetch({url}) = [read(net(host))], or "unknown" when the URL has no host (src/effects.ts:206-220)

as_told_to_model.text: Fields: url, host, method, credentials, rendered. Use === only.

sh.where: src/shell/sh-call.ts:215-235 (interface ShFacts), 247-288 (shFacts builder), 199 (ShPathFact), 203-208 (placeAmongRoots); passed as c by src/sw/sw-shell-call.ts:210-211 (asPolicyFacts), judged at 146, 223, 284

fields.program: { path: string, inRoot: boolean, version: string | null }
fields.cwd: { path: string, inRoot: boolean, topLevel?: boolean, isRoot?: boolean, containsSecret?: boolean | null }
fields.paths: { arg: number, given: string, path: string, inRoot: boolean, secret: boolean, exists: boolean, topLevel?: boolean, isRoot?: boolean, containsSecret?: boolean | null, sha256?: string | null }[]
fields.effects: EffectSet view (from the program manifest via describeCall, src/shell/program-manifest.ts:154; "unknown" when no manifest, a version mismatch, an entrypoint miss or a non-free env)

sh.notes: NO kind field on sh facts (c.kind in an sh policy is a refusal). topLevel/isRoot present only when roots were given; containsSecret/sha256 only when the host sent them. The probe judgement at sw-shell-call.ts:283-284 uses shFacts(probe) with effects: []. docs/spec/SHELL.md's field table lists a `run` field and describes `program` as a resolved file; neither matches: there is no `run`, and program is an object, so the POLICIES.md:71 example /git/.test(c.program) would test "[object Object]"-like coercion, not the path.
